test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The speed of a boat in still water is 13 km/h and the speed of the stream is 4 km/h. How much more time will it take in going upstream than in going downstream a distance of 68 km? (Correct to the nearest minute)
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the boat in still water = 13 km/h.

Speed of the stream = 4 km/h.

Distance = 68 km.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed.

Speed upstream = (Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream).

Speed downstream = (Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream).

**Calculation:**

Speed upstream = 13 - 4 = 9 km/h.

Speed downstream = 13 + 4 = 17 km/h.

Time taken upstream = 68 / 9.

⇒ Time taken upstream = 7.555... hours.

Time taken downstream = 68 / 17.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 4 hours.

Difference in time = Time taken upstream - Time taken downstream.

⇒ Difference in time = 7.555... - 4 = 3.555... hours.

Convert 3.555... hours to minutes.

⇒ Difference in time = 3 hours + (0.555... × 60) minutes.

⇒ Difference in time = 3 hours + 33.33 minutes ≈ 3 hours 33 minutes.

**The correct option is 3 (3 hours 33 minutes).**
